CEST-detectable metabolite candidates: myocardium

3 of 6 candidates clear the simulated with-vs-without contrast threshold (0.5%) at some field strength, by chemical exchange (downfield, +ppm) or by the relayed NOE (upfield, −ppm). 0 fall below it; 3 are unknown because no group had a verified reference rate, so nothing could be simulated. The threshold applies to our own simulation, never to a literature MTRasym.

  • Phosphocreatine: ✓ detectable (chemical exchange)
  • Glycogen (glucosyl unit): ✓ detectable (rNOE)
  • Mobile Protein/Peptide Amide Pool: ✓ detectable (both)
  • Taurine: ? unknown (not simulated)
  • Glutamate: ? unknown (not simulated)
  • Alanine: ? unknown (not simulated)

Excluded before simulation (not stored in the tissue): [model's own exclusion] Glutamine (myocardium releases rather than accumulates; concentrations low, typically <1 mM); [model's own exclusion] Lactate (typically <1 mM in healthy myocardium at rest, rises during ischemia); [model's own exclusion] Free Creatine (typically <1 mM; PCr is dominant form, ~80-85% of total creatine); [model's own exclusion] Glycosaminoglycans/GAGs (concentrations far below 1 mM in myocardium; primarily cartilage/disc target); [model's own exclusion] Phosphomonoesters/PDE/Total Choline (spectroscopic groupings, not chemically defined molecules/polymers); [model's own exclusion] 31P MRS-only peaks (e.g., inorganic phosphate, ATP gamma/beta) without identified 1H exchangeable proton pools

Phosphocreatine — CEST: ✓ detectable (chemical exchange)

Concentration: 13.00 mM typical (10-18) animal evidence only

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: Myocardial total creatine (Cr + PCr) is consistently reported in biochemistry literature as approximately 15-20 mmol/kg wet weight in healthy euthyroid hearts, with phosphocreatine comprising approximately 80-85% of this pool. Deriving PCr from these consensus values: 17 mmol/kg total * 0.83 = 14.1 mmol/kg. This is an estimate based on standard textbook/consensus values for total creatine rather than a direct single-paper measurement of PCr alone, as most studies report total creatine or the PCr/ATP ratio via 31P MRS. PCr contains exchangeable amine protons on the guanidino group.

Derivation stepValueSource
Total creatine (free creatine + phosphocreatine) in healthy euthyroid myocardium is approximately 15-20 mmol/kg wet weight.17 mmol/kg (midpoint)reference_work: Standard cardiac biochemistry references and 31P MRS literature consensus (e.g., reviews in PMID 7808461, PMID 3888084)
Phosphocreatine constitutes approximately 80-85% of total creatine in healthy myocardium.0.83reference_work: Standard cardiac biochemistry references and 31P MRS literature consensus (e.g., reviews in PMID 7808461, PMID 3888084)
Phosphocreatine concentration is calculated as total creatine multiplied by the PCr fraction.17 * 0.83 = 14.1 mmol/kgcalculation

Recommended field strength(s): 1.5 T, 3 T, 5 T, 7 T

Robustness to input uncertainty: robust

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (Guanidinium NH [guanidinium]: concentration 10-18 mM, kex 80-290 s−1) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.10-0.18%, 1.5 T: 0.32-0.74%, 3 T: 0.61-1.42%, 5 T: 0.72-2.15%, 7 T: 0.82-2.49%. Threshold 0.5%. Detectable even at the low corner.

Frequency-collision analysis: At 0.5 T, PCr (2.6 ppm) and Amide (3.5 ppm) are separated by only 19.2 Hz, less than the combined exchange-broadened linewidth (~72 Hz). They blur into one peak. At 3 T and above, separation >270 Hz, resolving them. MTRasym at low fields will be contaminated by Amide signal.

Direct water saturation: Direct saturation bandwidths (21-43 Hz) are much smaller than the PCr offset (520-1300 Hz) at all fields. No direct water saturation overlap masks the PCr contrast.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: The exchange rate (185 s−1) is borrowed from human calf muscle in vivo. Myocardial pH and microenvironment differ. Guanidinium exchange is pH-sensitive; ischemic acidosis could alter kex significantly, affecting optimal B1 and contrast magnitude. Confidence is reduced by this borrowing.

Optimized saturation sequence by field strength (derived from a Bloch-McConnell B1×Tsat sweep):

  • 0.5 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=500 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.143% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 1.5 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=1500 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.560% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 3 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Intermediate exchange (kex ~185). Requires moderate B1 to drive saturation without causing direct water saturation or excessive Amide cross-saturation. 3s allows signal buildup.
    recommended sequence: 1.076% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 5 T: B1=1 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Higher field allows higher B1 for intermediate exchange pools. Peak contrast shifts to higher B1. 3s saturation time is optimal.
    recommended sequence: 1.475% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 7 T: B1=1 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Similar to 5T. High field improves resolution from Amide. B1 1.0 µT is optimal for kex ~185 at 7T.
    recommended sequence: 1.694% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied

B1/Tsat vs. extraction method (click for note + literature)

Note: Multi-pool Lorentzian fitting or FASTAEX fitting is required at 3T to separate PCr from Amide. Simple MTRasym is risky below 3T due to overlap. At 7T, MTRasym is more acceptable but fitting is superior.

No citations.

Potential clinical impact

amine (PCrCEST, 2.0 ppm; 31P-MRS PCr): 0 CEST/NOE application and 3 metabolite-change studies verified (2 human, 1 animal; 33 humans, 0 animals; 2 dropped by verification). No CEST studies found for PCr in myocardial disease. Strong 31P-MRS evidence shows reduced PCr and PCr/ATP ratio in myocardial infarction and heart failure across human and animal models, indicating impaired myocardial energetics.

Caveats / critique (6 points, 284 words) — Concentration of 13 mM is standard for healthy myocardium but drops significantly during ischemia (down to <5 mM). Simulated contrast is optimal for healthy tis…
  • Concentration of 13 mM is standard for healthy myocardium but drops significantly during ischemia (down to <5 mM). Simulated contrast is optimal for healthy tissue; pathological states will yield lower contrast proportional to concentration drop. Group class 'guanidinium' is correct. The chemist's estimated shift of 3.2 ppm was incorrect; simulation uses 2.6 ppm based on literature medians.
  • This correction prevents fatal overlap with Amide (3.5 ppm) at low fields. No other exchangeable protons neglected. Simulated shift 2.6 ppm. Literature confirms ~2.6 ppm for PCr guanidinium protons in muscle in vivo. This is distinct from the chemist's initial 3.2 ppm estimate. None. Phosphate protons exchange too fast/invisible. Amide-like NH are the only relevant CEST-active protons.
  • verifying_citations: PMID 32179431 (claimed as 'In vivo 31P MRS and CEST characterization of phosphocreatine and creatine in human muscle') dropped PubMed's actual title is 'Amplified detection of phosphocreatine and creatine after supplementation using CEST MRI at high and ultrahigh magnetic fields.'. verifying_citations: PMID 36161668 (claimed as 'Steady-state CEST with MR multitasking reveals metabolic changes in human liver') dropped
  • PubMed's actual title is 'Free-breathing 3D CEST MRI of human liver at 3.0\xa0T.'. extraction_method_citations: PMID 26334509 (claimed as 'Quantitative CEST in human liver') dropped PubMed's actual title is 'Chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) MR technique for in-vivo liver imaging at 3.0 tesla.'.
  • no SAR or hardware ceiling is applied: the recommended B1/Tsat is the sweep optimum, and deliverability must be checked against the scanner's SAR monitor PCr has exchangeable protons on the amine group.
  • While primarily a 31P MRS target, the amine protons are chemically exchangeable and could contribute to 1H CEST contrast, though this is less commonly studied than glycoCEST or APT.

Recommended field strength(s): 3 T, 5 T, 7 T

Robustness to input uncertainty: fragile

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (Aliphatic C-H (rNOE) [rnoe]: concentration 3.7-46.3 mM, kex fixed at 5 s−1 (single measurement, spread unknown)) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.02-0.28%, 1.5 T: 0.05-0.61%, 3 T: 0.08-1.02%, 5 T: 0.10-1.24%, 7 T: 0.11-1.35%. Threshold 0.5%. Only the point estimate clears the threshold; the low corner does not.

Frequency-collision analysis: OH (+1.0 ppm) is isolated from other CEST pools. rNOE (-1.1 ppm) overlaps with MT tail at low fields (0.5-1.5T). At 7T, separation from MT is 387 Hz, allowing resolution.

Direct water saturation: No direct saturation overlap. Offsets are far from water (1.0 ppm and -1.1 ppm).

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: Hydroxyl kex (31,850 s−1) from phantom. This is very fast, explaining low OH contrast. rNOE kex (5 s−1) from generic protein phantoms. In vivo rNOE may be stronger due to macromolecular mobility. Hydroxyl is undetectable; rNOE is the viable target.

Optimized saturation sequence by field strength (derived from a Bloch-McConnell B1×Tsat sweep):

  • 0.5 T: B1=0.1 µT, Tsat=2000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.184% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 1.5 T: B1=0.1 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.397% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 3 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — rNOE is slow exchange (kex ~5). Low B1 (0.25 µT) is optimal to maximize transfer efficiency and avoid direct saturation. 3s saturation allows buildup.
    recommended sequence: 0.659% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 5 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Same physics as 3T. Low B1 preferred for rNOE. Contrast increases with field.
    recommended sequence: 0.804% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 7 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Same physics. Low B1 is critical for rNOE. High field improves separation from MT.
    recommended sequence: 0.878% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied

Mobile Protein/Peptide Amide Pool — CEST: ✓ detectable (both)

Concentration: 91.00 mM typical (50-100) animal evidence only

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: This is an estimate based on typical total protein content in myocardium (~200 mg protein/g wet weight = 200 g/L) and the fraction that is mobile/accessible to CEST. The repeating unit is the peptide backbone amide group. Assuming ~1 amide proton per amino acid residue, and an average amino acid MW of ~110 Da, total amide concentration is ~200 g/L / 110 g/mol = ~1.8 M (1820 mM) if all protein were mobile and contributing. The 'mobile' fraction contributing to APT is much smaller, typically estimated at a few percent of total protein in MRS/CEST contexts (as the solid-like macromolecular matrix does not exchange fast enough for CEST). A typical APT signal corresponds to an effective amide proton concentration in the tens of millimolar range. I am estimating 50-100 mM for the mobile amide pool based on general APT literature in soft tissues, acknowledging this is a rough order-of-magnitude estimate specific to the mobile fraction, not total protein.

Frequency-collision analysis: Amide (+3.5 ppm) overlaps with PCr (+2.6 ppm) at 1.5T (separation 57.5 Hz vs linewidth 71.7 Hz). Resolved at 3T+. rNOE (-3.5 ppm) overlaps with MT (-2.4 ppm) at low fields. Resolved at 7T.

Direct water saturation: No direct saturation overlap. Offset 3.5 ppm is far from water relative to B1 bandwidths.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: kex 65.5 s−1 borrowed from brain. Myocardial protein environment differs, but kex range (15-158 s−1) covers likely values. Acidosis in ischemia slows kex, potentially increasing contrast.

Glutamate — CEST: ? unknown (not simulated)

Concentration: 2.00 mM typical (1.5-3.0) animal evidence only

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: Glutamate is a major TCA cycle intermediate and neurotransmitter/amino acid in heart. While I could not find a direct quote of myocardial glutamate concentration in mM, it is a standard metabolite in heart extracts analyzed by NMR (PMID 33900680). In skeletal muscle and liver, glutamate concentrations are typically 1-3 mM. Given the heart's high metabolic rate and glutamate's role in nitrogen shuttling and anaplerosis, a concentration of ~2 mM is a reasonable estimate for the mobile cytosolic/mitochondrial pool. Glutamate has exchangeable protons on the alpha-amino and side-chain amide/carboxyl groups (though carboxyl OH are often not observable by CEST due to fast exchange/pKa). The alpha-amino and amide NH2 protons are exchangeable.

In vivo verification: ROI-differential CEST scan — Short-axis (oblique axial perpendicular to LV long axis)

Why this scan: Myocardium has distinct protein and PCr concentrations vs skeletal muscle and negligible glycogen vs liver/spleen. Comparing Z-spectra across Myocardium, Paraspinal Muscle, and Subcutaneous Fat isolates metabolite-specific contrast from generic MT/NOE, which scales poorly with these specific metabolic differences.

ROIWhere it is drawnRole
Myocardium target tissueMid-wall of left ventricular free wall and septum, avoiding blood pool and fat.Target tissue with high protein, PCr, and glycogen.
Paraspinal MusclePosterior intercostal/paraspinal muscle bulk in the same slice FOV.Comparison: Higher PCr/protein, lower glycogen than myocardium.
Subcutaneous FatAnterior chest wall subcutaneous adipose tissue.Reference: Negligible PCr/glycogen/protein amide signal.
SpleenSplenic parenchyma visible in inferior aspect of slice or adjacent base.Comparison: High protein, low PCr/glycogen.

Scan protocol: 3 T, pulsed rectangular train, B1=0.75 µT, 12 pulses × 50 ms (interpulse delay 200 ms, duty cycle 20%), total Tsat=3000 ms, TR=5000 ms

SAR reasoning (the experimentalist agent's own; the pipeline applies no SAR model): 16.7% duty cycle at 0.75 µT is low SAR. 3s saturation fits well within clinical limits for a single short-axis slice, minimizing thermal buildup.

Compromise rationale: 0.75 µT/3s optimizes slow-exchange amide (3.3 ppm) and intermediate-exchange PCr (3.2 ppm). It oversaturates relative to slow-exchange glycogen (1.2 ppm, optimal ~0.25 µT), reducing glycogen contrast but maintaining specificity via ROI differential.

Fat suppression: SPIR prepulse. Essential to suppress epicardial and subcutaneous fat signals that otherwise bleed into myocardium ROI and interfere with upfield glycogen/rNOE detection.

Motion mitigation: ECG-triggered acquisition at mid-diastole (70-80% RR) to freeze myocardial motion. Breath-hold discouraged due to long scan time; multi-shot gating used.

Slice coverage: Single 8mm short-axis slice centered on mid-LV myocardium. Perpendicular to LV long axis.

Structures in FOV: myocardium, paraspinal muscle, subcutaneous fat, spleen, liver

Z-spectrum sampling offsets:

  • -8.00 ppm: far-off baseline reference
  • -3.50 ppm: rNOE aliphatic
  • -1.00 ppm: rNOE glycogen
  • +0.00 ppm: water (0 ppm)
  • +1.20 ppm: Glycogen (glucosyl unit)
  • +3.20 ppm: Phosphocreatine
  • +3.30 ppm: Mobile Protein/Peptide Amide Pool
  • +8.00 ppm: far-off baseline reference

Differential analysis plan: Compare MTRasym(3.3 ppm) and MTRasym(3.2 ppm). Amide should scale: Myo (91) > Para (85) > Spleen (70) > Fat (5). PCr should scale: Para (30) > Myo (13) > Spleen (5) > Fat (0.5). Glycogen at 1.2 ppm: Myo (30) > Para (15) > Spleen (2) > Fat (0). Distinct ROI ordering at 3.2 vs 3.3 ppm confirms distinct pools.

Not actively targeted: Taurine, Glutamate, Alanine excluded due to low simulated contrast (<0.1%) and overlap with background MT/NOE, making them undetectable with this protocol.

Caveats (8 points, 316 words) — Partial volume effects in thin myocardium. B0/B1 inhomogeneity across FOV requires robust WASSR correction. Compromise B1 under-saturates glycogen, reducing its…

  • tsat_choice: grid Tsat with the highest contrast at the best B1 (no scan-time shortening)
  • pool_t1_s: 1.0
  • pool_t2_s: 0.01
  • max_background_metabolites: 3
  • verification_scan_field_T: 3.0
  • verification_scan_model: the experimentalist's pulse train (rectangular pulses at its B1), 90 degree single-shot readout, exact periodic steady state at its TR, Z normalized to the same cycle without saturation
  • b1_inhomogeneity_fraction: 0.3
  • uncertainty_corners: contrast re-simulated at the swept B1/Tsat at every corner of [concentration range from the literature agent] x [kex spread of the reference tier]
  • llm_sampling: each model's served defaults; the pipeline sends no temperature or top_p

A FAILED completeness check means the agent's structured output never covered everything it was asked to (e.g. a verdict for every metabolite) within its retry budget, and the incomplete output was kept; the deterministic checks above flag what is missing.
